dedupe_keys.name: california geological survey borehole database liquefaction boreholes

description: The California Geological Survey borehole database gives access to geotechnical boreholes used in the state's seismic hazard zonation, particularly for earthquake-induced liquefaction, with borehole locations and related tables of subsurface data. It is produced by the California Geological Survey in the Department of Conservation. Coverage is the areas of California mapped for liquefaction hazard zones. Users select boreholes on an interactive map with circle, box or polygon tools, about 50 at a time for good performance, and download the records and related tables as CSV files, free after accepting a disclaimer; the page read does not state a licence. Caveats: CGS calls the database an interim product while it develops a longer-term system, boreholes are concentrated where zonation was done, and logs come from many consultants and dates. For simulation it supplies soil profiles and penetration data for liquefaction and ground-shaking analyses of pipelines, roads, bridges and ports, and for hazard exposure and resilience studies of lifelines in California. It is related to the Nova Scotia Drillhole Database and USDA Web Soil Survey records in this catalogue, which give other kinds of subsurface data.
